boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the District of Eastern Arkansas and the District of Arkansas without counts; the live field reads zero. Holmes reports his whole force at 7,646; Greene says that with officers it was probably 8,000 to 9,000, that Union officers estimated it at 15,000, and that Prentiss's garrison numbered 4,129. NPS says the Confederates had more troops.
claims.rationale: Reported, estimated and garrison figures differ in scope; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Greene says Helena had been fortified by Fort Curtis and four outlying batteries commanding the western roads. Holmes says the place proved far more difficult of access and more strongly fortified than he had supposed, with one heavily armed regular work and four redoubts with rifle-pits on hills peculiarly adapted to defense.

claims.value: Holmes blames L. M. The live heading ranks Prentiss Brigadier General against the frozen Major General.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,842 total (US 206; CS 1,636); the live field reads 1875 total (US 239; CS 1636;). Holmes reports 173 killed, 687 wounded and 776 missing, 1,636 in all; Greene says Prentiss certified 400 buried, 108 wounded paroled and 993 prisoners sent north, 1,501 left in his hands, and gives the Union loss as 230.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Three Union figures (206, 239, 230) differ; the Confederate 1,636 agrees across frozen, live and Holmes.

open_questions: Prentiss's, Salomon's, Price's, Fagan's and Marmaduke's reports and the McRae court of inquiry remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
